hunts.label: Saturday, Nov 28
hunts.subtitle: Leftovers in the fridge, sun on the pines, and the squirrels never heard it was a holiday weekend.

rules.title: Saturday, Nov 28
items: **Crow is open today** (Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday only).
**Dove: last day of this segment.** Open to Nov 28, bag 15. It reopens Dec 16.
**Snipe is open** (to Feb 27, bag 8). Dove and snipe need HIP registration and a 3-shell plug.
**Woodcock is CLOSED** until Dec 10. Look and learn, do not shoot.
**Ducks and geese: skip them.** You carry lead shells, and waterfowl need nontoxic shot. Rails closed Nov 25.
**Hunter orange is required** (deer gun season is open to Jan 1). Your deer is done, but others are out.
rules.note: Confirm seasons and rules in the current NCWRC Regulations Digest before you go.

items: Walk-in about **42F**, feels near 37F (backup hourly forecast). The NWS overnight low is about 39F.
9 am about **48F** (backup hourly). The day reaches about **58F**.
Wind: **W 7 to 11 mph** (NWS). The hourly backup shows **WSW 8 to 11** from 4 to 9 am. No gusts listed.
Sky and rain: **sunny and dry**. A few early clouds clear around 7. Rain chance 4 percent or less.
Sunrise **6:57 am**. Legal light **6:27 am** (sunrise minus 30 minutes).
Moon: **waning gibbous**. Still up for the whole hunt, setting late morning.
conditions.meaning: Assumption: a cold, clear, dry morning after a bright night. Squirrels should be moving from first light and may pick up as the sun warms the treetops between 7:00 and 8:30. Rabbits likely sit tight in sunny cover out of the west wind. Snipe, if any, will be on soft mud where the storm water has pulled back.
conditions.hours_note: Hourly figures come from a backup weather page, not the National Weather Service, whose hourly table was out of date.

in_season.tip: Steady game today. Watch feed trees, then the sunlit crowns.
Thick cover near the feed bins and trail edges.
No covey seen here yet. Bonus only.
Walk the soft mud along the swamp.
North sky only, from the Junction.
Watch flight lines over the swamp.

in_season: Raccoon and opossum are open. Take only a sure, close shot.
Bear is closed until Dec 12. Bobcat is open but you do not hunt it.
Deer: tag filled for the season. Do not shoot a deer.

plan.title: Slope Top Seat, then a snipe walk
plan.why: A new seat **west of the Junction, at the top of the north slope**, where the ground starts to drop toward the swamp. Pick a **wide live trunk** within shotgun range of food: pine cone cuttings, holly, or an oak or hickory. Face **north-northwest, down the slope**. The ground below you makes a good backstop for low shots. The west wind comes over your left side and carries your scent right, toward the Junction side, away from what you watch. The sun rises behind your right shoulder and lights the trunks ahead. If you know a round hollow at the top of that slope, its rim is a fine landmark; sit where you can see over it. Then you move **into the wind** for a second sit, and walk the swamp edge for snipe. Every shot from the seat goes between WNW and NNE.

steps.text: Leave the yard on the main trail. Red light only. Gun unloaded, orange on. Watch overhead for limbs the storm left hanging.
At the Junction turn west and go 40 to 60 steps along the top of the slope. Sit against a live trunk facing NNW. Load #4, plug in. Light off.
Legal light. Sit still. Scan the ground, then trunks low to high, 20 to 35 yards out.
Sunrise. Watch the treetops as the sun reaches them. Look for shaking twigs and falling cuttings.
If quiet for 20 minutes, unload and slip about 60 steps west, into the wind. Sit again, same facing. Reload.
Unload and go down to the swamp edge. Load #7.5. Walk east toward the Junction with the wind at your back. Stop every few steps. Shots N over the swamp only. No woodcock.
Junction: stand with your back to a pine for 10 minutes. Watch the north sky for crow and dove.
Unload. Take the loop trail to the feed bins. Load, then kick rabbit cover. Shots N or NW only. Never toward the field SE or house SW.
Unload and count shells. Walk out by the loop and main trail, doing the land task.
Out at the yard. Clean and cool any game within the hour.

items: **In the gun: #4** (plug in) for both seats and the feed bins. Squirrel, rabbit, and crow to 35 yards.
**Right pocket: #7.5** for the snipe walk, dove, a close rabbit, or a quail flush.
**Slugs: zipped in a separate pocket.** Bear defense only.
**No 00 buckshot carried.**
**Choke: Modified.** Fine for everything today.
**.22 LR (optional):** head shots on a still squirrel only, with a trunk or the ground certain behind it. Never at a bird in the sky.
Pack - GRAB: gun, phone, water bottle filled, tell someone your plan and return time.
Pack - CHARGE: headlamp and spare flashlight before bed.
Pack - RESTOCK after the hunt: water, coffee or tea, nibble, nitrile gloves, .22 LR count, fatwood.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot. Not with #4, not with #7.5.
No ducks or geese with these shells. Lead shot is illegal for waterfowl.
Know the bird before you shoot. A woodcock can flush from the same wet ground as a snipe, and it is closed.

animals.name: Gray squirrel and fox squirrel
paragraphs: The most common game here. Grays work pines, holly, oaks, and hickories. A fox squirrel may show in the pines.
Cold, sunny, and dry today: expect movement from first light, with more in the treetops once the sun hits them.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 at 20 to 35 yards, head and neck.
Wait for it to stop with a trunk or the ground behind it.
With the .22 LR, take only a still squirrel against a trunk or the ground.

details.title: Technique: sit, move, sit
steps: Sit 20 to 30 minutes without moving.
If nothing shows, unload and creep about 60 steps into the wind.
Sit again and wait at least 15 minutes before you judge the spot.
Use your monocular on odd bumps along limbs.

after: Tip: look for what is level and lumpy on a limb. A resting squirrel often looks like a knot with an ear.
Tip: low sun throws shadows. A moving shadow on a trunk can show a squirrel you cannot see.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: Cottontails use thick holly, briars, brush, and the weedy cover by the feed bins.
After a cold night, check cover that gets sun and blocks the west wind: its east and south sides.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 or #7.5 at 15 to 25 yards, head and front shoulders.
Shoot only with the ground behind the rabbit.
Never shoot toward the south line or the field SE.

details.title: Technique: set the escape lane
steps: Before you kick, look for the likely way out: a run or gap in the cover.
Stand so that lane leads N or NW.
Kick once, then wait 30 seconds with the gun ready.
If it runs south, let it go.

after: Tip: check the tangled tops of any limbs the storm brought down. Fresh cover draws rabbits.

animals.name: Quail (bonus)
paragraphs: Northern bobwhite. No covey has been seen here. Look where thick brush meets weedy openings and bare dirt.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5, one bird at a time.
Shoot only birds flying N, W, or E.

details.title: Technique: listen after a flush
steps: If a covey scatters, stop and stay quiet.
Listen for soft whistles as birds call to regroup.
On a cold day, leave them to get back together.

after: Tip: look for a tight ring of droppings on the ground. It marks a night roost.

animals.name: Snipe
paragraphs: A bird of open soft mud. As Thursday's storm water drops, new mud edges may appear along the swamp. Not yet confirmed here.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5, inside 30 yards.
Let the first zig-zag pass, then swing through.
Shots N only, over the swamp.

details.title: Technique: wind at your back
steps: Walk the mud edge east today.
Snipe tend to rise into the wind, which slows them for a moment.
Pause every few steps. A stop often flushes a bird that was holding.
details.note: If the bird swings south, hold fire.

after: Tip: a harsh, raspy call on the flush points to snipe.

animals.name: Dove
paragraphs: Mourning doves pass over open edges and water. Today is the last day until Dec 16. A bonus, not the plan.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: Sky shots to the north only.

details.title: Technique: range markers
steps: At the Junction, pick two trees about 30 yards out.
Shoot only birds that pass inside that distance.
Swing through and follow through.

after: Tip: on a cold sunny morning, doves may warm up on high bare limbs. Watch which way they leave.

animals.name: Crow
paragraphs: Crows travel over the swamp in the morning. Open today.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 to 35 yards, #7.5 inside 25 yards.
Open sky to the north only.

details.title: Call: hail caw
steps: From pine shadow, give two long, slow caws.
Wait two full minutes and watch.
If a crow answers and turns, stop calling and hold still.

after: Tip: keep your face shaded under your hat brim until you decide to shoot.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Both live here. At dawn one may still be walking home to a hollow tree along the swamp.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 to the head at 20 yards or less, ground or trunk behind.
Confirm it is dead before you touch it. Wear gloves.
details.note: Leave any animal that acts sick or dazed.

after: Tip: a den tree opening with worn bark and caught hair is likely in use. Mark it.

animals.name: Bear and bobcat
paragraphs: Awareness only. Bear season is closed until Dec 12. Give a bear space, talk out loud, and back away. Slugs are for defense only.

skill.title: Woodcock and snipe: tell them apart, then shoot the flush
skill.principle: Two long-billed birds, two kinds of ground, two seasons. **Identify first.** Snipe is open today. Woodcock is closed until Dec 10 (to Jan 30, bag 3).

sections.title: Tell them apart
steps: Ground: snipe use open wet mud and grassy edges. Woodcock use damp thickets with soft soil under cover.
Shape: snipe is slim. Woodcock is plump and round with large eyes set high.
Head: snipe stripes run front to back. Woodcock bars run across the crown.
Belly: snipe is white. Woodcock is warm buff orange.
Flush: snipe zig-zags low and fast with a raspy call. Woodcock rises steeply with twittering wings.

sections.title: Read the sign
steps: Look for clusters of small round probe holes in soft ground.
Look for white chalky splashes on leaves under thick cover. That points to woodcock.
Open mud with probe holes and thin three-toed tracks points to snipe.

sections.title: Shoot the flush
steps: Carry at port arms, muzzle up, safety on. Know your N shooting lane before each step.
Walk a few steps, then stop for 5 to 10 seconds.
When a bird rises, look for color, shape, and flight. If unsure, do not shoot.
Snipe: mount smoothly and shoot as the zig-zag straightens.
From Dec 10, woodcock: shoot as it tops out its climb and begins to level.
Mark the fall against a stump or tree and walk straight to it.

details.title: Why the pause works
paragraphs: A holding bird trusts its camouflage while you keep walking. When the steps stop, it often decides it has been seen and flies. Stopping also puts your feet where you can shoot from.

skill.checkpoint: After the swamp walk, say which bird each patch of ground suits: open mud for snipe, damp thicket for woodcock. Log both with a note:.

land.intro: Map the ground for the Dec 10 woodcock opener while you hunt snipe.
steps: On the swamp walk, mark any open mud with probe holes. Pace it from the Junction.
On the walk out, find one damp, thick patch with soft soil. Look for probe holes and white splashes.
Note any squirrel den hole or leaf nest you saw from the slope seat.
Send it with a note: message, for example: note: probe holes 30 paces W of the Junction, damp holly patch on the loop, 2 leaf nests by the slope seat.

safety: NEVER shoot south. The house is SW and the field is SE: no-shoot directions.
From both slope seats, shoot only between WNW and NNE, with the ground or a trunk behind the animal.
At the feed bins, shoot N or NW only. If the line leans toward the house, hold fire.
Sky shots at crow and dove only to the north, over the swamp.
Hunter orange hat and vest are required (Oct 17 to Jan 1). Deer gun season is still open for other hunters.
The slope and swamp edge may still be wet and slick from Thursday's storm. Unload before you go down the slope or cross logs.
Feels near 37F. Keep hands warm enough to work the safety. Watch for hung limbs overhead.
hunts.regs: Check seasons, bag limits, and the crow, dove, and snipe rules in the current NCWRC Regulations Digest before you hunt.
hunts.gaps: The NWS hourly table was out of date (October data), so the hourly chart, walk-in and 9 am temperatures come from a backup weather page. It shows a high of 61F and WSW wind; NWS shows 58F and W. Neither lists gusts for the morning. The usual sunrise page could not be opened. The sunrise time is from the backup page, which also shows 6:56. That page gives conflicting moon figures: 73 and 83 percent lit, and moonset 10:20 or 11:05 am. Goose zone dates for this land were not confirmed.
